newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian ANZ job ads rise 3.3 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Australian ANZ job ads rise 3.3 pct in Jan.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group said that its job advertisement series for January rose a seasonally adjusted 3.3 percent, more than erasing the downwardly revised 2.3 percent fall recorded in December.

This was the second increase in three months and the largest monthly gain since January last year. In trend terms, job ads rose by 0.1 percent, the first increase for two years but was still 12.9 percent down on January 1996.
Saul Eslake, chief economist at ANZ, said the data needed to be treated cautiously but added: "It does appear the two-year decline in the demand for labour may be coming to an end."
"January's increase needs to be interpreted cautiously because as we stressed last month, the level of job ads is traditionally very volatile around the summer holiday period," Eslake said.

He noted the number of job ads also rose sharply in January 1996 causing what looked to be an upturn in the trend series. That turned out to be a false signal and ads then fell by 13 percent over the following three months.
"Recent movements in the number of job advertisements are broadly in consistent with net new job creation averaging around 12,000 per month over the next three months," he said.
This was down on the average of 18,200 seen in the last three months of 1996, although more than two-thirds of these were part time jobs and total hours worked declined, said Eslake.
Employment needed to rise by an average 21,000 a month from January to June if the government's forecasts of 1.5 percent jobs growth for 1996/97 was to be met, Eslake added.
ANZ said previously released ads data had been revised following an annual seasonal re-analysis of the series by the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
January labour force data are due on Thursday. The unemployment rate was 8.6 percent in December.
